title: hive bot status output (v1)
description: Stable contract emitted by `hive bot status --json`. The SuccessPayload reports whether the Telegram bot process is running, its PID, and uptime (exit 0 when running, 1 when not). The ErrorPayload arm carries usage errors for the whole `hive bot` command surface — every `hive bot ... --json` usage error (missing/unknown subcommand, or a flag passed to a subcommand that does not accept it) rides this schema (exit 64).

running.description: Whether a live bot process holds the PID file.

pid.description: PID of the running bot, or null when running=false.

uptime_sec.description: Seconds since the PID file was written, or null when running=false.

pid_file.description: Absolute path of the bot PID file.

log_file.description: Absolute path of the bot JSON-line log file.

service_installed.description: Whether the per-user autostart unit file exists on disk (non-mutating probe). Always present; null only if the probe itself could not run.

service_enabled.description: Whether the service manager reports the autostart unit as enabled/loaded (non-mutating probe). Always present; null only if the probe itself could not run.

unit_path.description: Absolute path of the autostart unit file; null on unsupported platforms or if the probe could not run.

error_class.description: Short name (no module prefix) of the Hive::Error subclass that was raised. Always "InvalidTaskPath" for the current usage-error paths. Matches every other hive-* error envelope.

error_kind.description: missing_subcommand = `hive bot` with no SUBCOMMAND. unknown_subcommand = SUBCOMMAND outside the start/stop/status/reload/tail/install set. wrong_subcommand_flag = a flag was passed to a subcommand that does not accept it (e.g., --force on `bot status`, or --foreground combined with --detach on `bot start`).

exit_code.description: Hive::ExitCodes. 64=USAGE — every bot usage error rides InvalidTaskPath (exit 64).
